summary:
Digital Farmers is an end-to-end precision agriculture intelligence platform that merges real-time satellite telemetry from the NASA POWER API with a robust machine learning model (Random Forest Classifier).

What we developed: An interactive, bilingual (English and Arabic RTL) Streamlit web dashboard that delivers 24-hour early warnings for thermal and drought crop stress, evaluates environmental risk factors, and provides customized crop rotation strategies based on regional soil types.

How it addresses the challenge: By bypassing the need for expensive ground hardware, the platform automates climate risk assessment using authentic NASA space data, translating complex satellite feeds into actionable, localized insights for everyday farmers.

Why it is important: It empowers agricultural communities to optimize water consumption, safeguard food security, and build climate resilience in an era of rapid environmental change.
details:
• What it does / How it works: Digital Farmers is an end-to-end precision agriculture platform that merges real-time satellite climate telemetry from the NASA POWER API with a robust Machine Learning model (Random Forest Classifier). The platform pulls live and historical agro-climatological data—including air temperature (T2M), precipitation (PRECTOTCORR), surface soil moisture (GWETTOP), and evapotranspiration (EVPTRNS)—for any global coordinates or pre-set agricultural hubs (such as the Nile Delta, Central Valley, and Punjab). A time-series shifted Machine Learning model analyzes these inputs to forecast 24-hour thermal and drought crop stress probabilities. Furthermore, the system features a bilingual (English / Arabic RTL) interactive Streamlit dashboard displaying historical seasonal trends, water balance charts, and custom CSV data exports.
    • Programming Language: Python.
    • Machine Learning & Data Processing: Scikit-Learn (Random Forest Algorithm), Pandas, NumPy, Joblib.
    • Frontend & Visualization: Streamlit framework combined with Plotly Express for high-performance interactive charts and bilingual UI support.
    • APIs & Data Source: NASA Langley Research Center (LaRC) POWER Project API (Agroclimatology / AG community endpoint).
  • Creativity & Design Factors Considered: The project bridges the gap between complex satellite space data and practical, everyday farming by introducing a localized Arabic-first (RTL) and English dual-language interface, making space tech accessible to regional farmers. We carefully balanced model accuracy with interpretability—evaluating primary environmental drivers (e.g., temperature and soil moisture dominance)—while designing a lightweight, self-hosted web architecture that runs smoothly without heavy cloud dependencies.
